story_angle.text: It's the world's biggest MPA—but no one has direct power to stop a fishing boat from entering it.
Regulations that do exist are hard to enforce and track

description.text: In the middle of the North Atlantic, between the Azores, the Grand Banks of Newfoundland, and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. It is entirely in international waters—
no country owns or controls it.
Scientists strapped trackers to 2,188 seabirds from 21 species across 56 colonies. The data revealed up to
—including puffins, arctic terns, and kittiwakes—flock to this ocean area each year to feed. It was the largest seabird concentration ever found on the open ocean.
When researchers looked at the seafloor below, they found
, ancient coral gardens, and deep-sea shark nurseries. In 2023, OSPAR expanded protection to cover the seabed too.

context.text: Here’s the catch: OSPAR,  the body that designated NACES, doesn’t control fishing or shipping. Those are governed by separate international bodies. So the MPA is a set of conservation objectives and political commitments, not a hard enforcement zone. In practice:

bullet_points.text: on seamounts is a major concern and is generally banned in the North Atlantic by the north-East Atlantic fisheries body (NEAFC)
for tuna and sharks (managed by ICCAT) is flagged as a threat
Seabird, turtle, and shark bycatch is a priority issue across all gear types
Deep-sea mining is handled through a separate body (the International Seabed Authority)
Shipping noise and pollution fall under the International Maritime Organization

agencies.name: OSPAR Commission
agencies.details: Designated the MPA. 16 members including the EU. Sets conservation objectives and calls on others to act.

agencies.name: NEAFC
agencies.details: North-East Atlantic fisheries body. OSPAR is asking NEAFC to translate MPA objectives into fishing restrictions.

agencies.name: ICCAT
agencies.details: Manages tuna and sharks in the Atlantic. Key body for addressing longline fishing impacts.

agencies.name: International Seabed Authority
agencies.details: Controls deep-sea mining licences in the Area (seabed beyond national jurisdiction).

. NACES and this treaty are deeply intertwined:

implications.text: NACES was created before the treaty existed
The treaty now gives the global community a proper legal framework to manage places like NACES
NACES is widely seen as the model for what the treaty can achieve at scale — a proof of concept
The big question: will the new treaty give teeth to an MPA that currently relies on voluntary cooperation?
